correctness.rationale: In any complete join of at least two noncomplete factors, each cross-factor vertex lies on a length-two geodesic joining any same-factor nonedge. A nonempty dual set must meet each factor or violate convexity of its complement. Using a chosen vertex in another factor forces both colors to be cliques within each factor. The converse and bijection with proper two-colorings of the complement are exact. Bipartite connected-component orientations give the full labelled polynomial, maximum and maximal configurations. The direct finite verifier independently tested 1,085 profiles and 139,216 subsets; infinite validity is established by the proof, not extrapolation.

originality.rationale: Specific full-join dual general-position characterization, count polynomial, inclusion-maximal formula and complete-first-factor lexicographic-product solution were not stated in inspected 2012 convexity, 2024 dual general-position and 2024 product works. The journal product paper explicitly leaves \(K_m\circ H\) undetermined; its zero and complete-second-factor cases do not imply the formula without a new cross-layer reasoning step. Earlier convexity and complete-multipartite special cases are properly acknowledged; independent priority is not claimed.

value.rationale: An explicit question about gp_d(\(K_m\circ H\)) in the closest product literature is solved for every finite H, with a complete labelled all-set polynomial and all inclusion-maximal configurations, and the theorem extends to nonuniform complete joins. The bipartite-complement threshold gives contrasting infinite families and a precise toggle-graph structure; these data are not merely routine numeric increments. The computation checks definitions but is not the primary motivation.
